title: The Last Tide
premise: Jonah Eriksen inherited her grandfather's failing vineyard along with his debts, and five years of careful, cautious rebuilding have taught her to trust no one — least of all the family who abandoned her. When a survey reveals that half of the stubborn old orchard legally belongs to Mara Voss, the estranged childhood friend whose family Jonah's grandfather wronged decades ago, the two women are forced into an uneasy partnership to save the harvest both need. As lawsuits, sabotage, and long-buried truths about the deed surface, Jonah must choose between protecting the vineyard's reputation and exposing what her grandfather really did, while falling for the orchard's quiet caretaker, Theo, who carries secrets of his own. In the end, Jonah testifies to the truth at the cost of half her land, forgives herself for the resentments she nursed, and finds that belonging was never something she could inherit — only something she could build.
about_author: Odile Joubert is a former sommelier who traded tasting rooms for writing desks and now lives above a cider house in coastal Oregon. Her novels explore how families are made, unmade, and remade in the spaces between forgiveness and truth.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Five years after inheriting the vineyard, Jonah counts her small safe wins: a repaired press, a paid-off loan, a first viable crop coming in. A letter from the county threatens it all with a boundary dispute. Emotional beat: guarded hope cracked by dread.

chapters.title: The Stubborn Deed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The county clerk shows her the original deed: half the orchard parcel lists a second name — Mara Voss, the friend who vanished from her life at seventeen. Jonah drives to the orchard gate and finds it padlocked against her. Emotional beat: betrayal resurfacing like a scar reopened.

chapters.title: A Woman at the Fence Line
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara has returned to claim her late mother's share of the orchard, needing the land sale to survive a divorce. She recognizes Jonah instantly and braces for old wounds. Their first meeting is cold, transactional, and charged. Emotional beat: two women armored in old grief.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept the Trees
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Theo Lindqvist, the orchard caretaker hired years ago by Mara's mother, refuses to let either woman neglect the trees mid-season. He offers to mediate; Jonah bristles but accepts help pruning. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth kindling in shared work.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Buried
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Searching the farmhouse attic for documents, Jonah finds her grandfather's ledger with payments marked 'V.' and a torn page. She realizes he may have cheated the Voss family deliberately. She hides the ledger. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning its war with truth.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A storm damages the orchard; Mara stays to help salvage the fruit despite herself. Working beside Theo and, awkwardly, Jonah, she remembers why she loved this valley. Emotional beat: homesickness she refused to name.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah offers Mara a buyout financed by a predatory lender, desperate to keep the whole property. Mara counters: co-ownership through one full season, then decide. Theo quietly endorses the plan. Emotional beat: pride wrestling with necessity.

chapters.title: Terms of Truce
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The co-ownership agreement is signed over cheap wine and stiffer silences. Mara unpacks in the old cottage and finds her mother's letters hinting at 'what Elias did.' Emotional beat: suspicion planted beside fragile peace.

chapters.title: First Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Frost threatens the vines; the three work through the night lighting smudge pots. Exhausted and laughing at dawn, Jonah feels something like family for the first time in years — and hates how much she wants it. Emotional beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: Theo's Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara notices Theo deflects every question about the year the Vosses left town. She catches him burning papers near the barn. When confronted, he says only, 'Ask your mother's lawyer.' Emotional beat: trust fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: The Ledger Opens
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Mara's lawyer subpoenas estate records; the hidden ledger will surface. Jonah confesses to Mara that she found it and hid it. Mara walks out. That night Jonah reads the full entries: her grandfather bought the Voss debt and forged the quitclaim. Emotional beat: shame turning inward.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Alone, Jonah confronts the pattern of her own life — every relationship abandoned before it could abandon her, every truth deferred. She drafts a letter of confession to the county and can't send it. Emotional beat: the beginning of self-forgiveness, unfinished.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Someone sprays defoliant on the orchard rows; the crop is crippled weeks before harvest. Suspicion falls on Jonah, whose truck was seen nearby. Mara wants to believe her innocence but the evidence stings. Emotional beat: alliance collapsing into accusation.

chapters.title: The Lender's Shadow
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah discovers the predatory lender she approached has been buying up distressed valley farms — and that his agent was the figure near her truck. Proof exists, but exposing him means revealing the forged deed publicly. Emotional beat: courage gathering against consequence.

chapters.title: Rain on the Cottage Roof
chapters.summary: Jonah and Mara alternating. Trapped together by a storm, they finally speak plainly: the night Mara left at seventeen, and the letter Jonah never sent. Old love and old hurt untangle into something honest. Emotional beat: reconciliation without absolution yet.

chapters.title: Theo Testifies
chapters.summary: Theo's POV (via Mara). Theo comes forward: Mara's mother hired him to protect evidence of the forgery until Mara was ready to return. His silence was loyalty to a dead woman's wish. He gives Mara the original quitclaim draft. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as love, not betrayal.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the county hearing, Jonah takes the stand and tells the whole truth — the ledger, the forgery, her concealment — surrendering any claim to the orchard half. The gallery goes silent; Mara's face is unreadable. Emotional beat: truth chosen over safety at last.

chapters.title: What the Land Decides
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The court restores Mara's title; the lender's fraud unravels, freeing Jonah's debts partially. Mara stands at the fence line holding the deed and the memory of Jonah's testimony. Emotional beat: justice arriving quieter than expected.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Harvest day arrives on both parcels. Mara arrives not with lawyers but with picking baskets, proposing a joint label: Last Tide, pressed from both properties. Theo smiles for the first time in chapters. Emotional beat: abundance earned together.

chapters.title: The Letter Sent
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah mails the confession letter she once couldn't send — now addressed to herself, read aloud at the farmhouse table with Mara and Theo as witnesses. Forgiveness of the person in the mirror finally lands. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Winter comes; the three share the first bottle of Last Tide in the restored farmhouse kitchen. Mara signs a new deed — not dividing the land but binding the partnership. Emotional beat: home chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Tide Comes Back
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, closing. Spring buds on the orchard; Jonah walks the fence line with no lock on the gate. She reflects that tides go out so they can return, and that she stayed. Final image: two names on one deed, neither estranged. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
